text:
jordan: Heads-up — support ticket: customer A's console is showing rows that belong to customer B in the Reserved Capacity table. https://support/pts/1245 (screenshot attached by support)
maria-g: wtf. any recent console changes that touch query/filtering or cache keys? :eyes:
eli: rolled the v2-query toggle to canary yesterday around 15:04 UTC, but only 10% orgs. that touches response caching and param handling.
raj: checking gateway logs now. i see queries where `workspace_id` is missing in the param but `X-Workspace` header is present. some handlers treat header as authoritative.
jordan: support repro steps: switch workspace via the UI, then quickly open the Reserved Capacity page. intermittent — appears right after switching.
sam: i repro locally by flipping workspaces fast. client keeps prior workspaceId in local state for ~200ms; the fetch uses header if present and cache layer keys by full query string. race -> wrong cache hit.
ira: from auth side: handler precedence is `header > param > session`. session isn't cleared on client switch, so when header is absent the stale session wins. we should not allow header to override authz without validation.
eli: tagging @eng-security — this is cross-tenant metadata exposure. need triage and telemetry to know scope. ops-bot: can you open an incident with high priority? :exclamation:
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-142 — "workspace-context-bleed". PagerDuty notified. Assigned to eng-platform oncall.
raj: proposed immediate mitigation: enforce an authz middleware in the gateway that rejects requests where requested workspace != authenticated org, and bypass cached hits unless the cache key includes the org id. add a 5xx guard for any cache key mismatch.
maria-g: also add an audit log event on any workspace mismatch attempt (request_id, user, attempted_workspace) so we can notify affected customers and satisfy compliance asks.
sam: i'll open a small PR for the middleware and a parallel PR to change cache keys. quick snippet of the cache change:
```
// old
cacheKey = req.path + "::" + req.querystring
// new
cacheKey = req.path + "::org=" + req.auth.orgId + "::" + req.querystring
```
sam: plan: patch -> staging (1h), run e2e focusing on workspace switch flappers, canary to 10% (2h), then full rollout after 24h if green. will include telemetry to count mismatches.
jordan: support messaging: tell impacted customers we isolated it to console UI cached rows and no model or tenant data was run against the wrong org. draft in #support-drafts and legal loop if needed.
ira: i'll handle the postmortem template and coordinate with product for the rollout UX fix: client should clear workspace state before navigation completes. UX change is low-risk but might need a small migration for older browsers.
eli: internal API debate: do we prohibit `X-Workspace` header entirely (safer) or require signed header tokens (more work)? leaning toward disallow and rely on explicit param/session.
raj: agree disallowing header by default is safest. if we ever need it for internal tooling, we can add a signed/internal-only header with strict validation.
maria-g: sounds good. please cc me on the PRs and the incident timeline. i'll prepare comms for infra and product about telemetry we need.
jordan: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for triage. update here with PR links and the incident runbook.
